newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit ends rangebound in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit ends rangebound in thin trading.

text.p: The ringgit was mildly weaker, but within a tight range at the end of Asian trading on Monday, dealers said.
They said the ringgit was subjected to mild selling in late afternoon trading as players squared up their positions due to holidays in London and New York, keeping trading subdued, dealers said.
"There was also some commercial demand out of Kuala Lumpur," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank in Kuala Lumpur.
But, volumes were extremely low as the market was focussed on dollar/majors, he said.
"There were also no new factors to trade on in the regionals. Thai baht was quiet so there was a spillover effect on other regionals," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
He said the market was focusing on the French elections, where losses for President Jacques Chirac's coalition was causing a mild selloff in the dollar/mark.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5015/25 to a dollar.
